raw_record.question_text: Mike sets the table for 8 people: The fork has to lie to the left and the knife to the right of the plate. For how many people is the cutlery set correctly?

method.method_draft: First read the image as a rectangular table with 8 place settings: three along the top edge, one on the left side, one on the right side, and three along the bottom edge. For each setting identify the gray plate, the fork symbol with tines, and the black knife. Read the text rule that a correct setting has the fork on the diner’s left side and the knife on the diner’s right side of the plate. Then evaluate each seat from the perspective of the person sitting there, not from the viewer’s fixed left/right: top-side diners face downward, bottom-side diners face upward, the left-side diner faces right, and the right-side diner faces left. Mark a setting correct if, after this rotation, fork is on the person’s left and knife on the person’s right. Counting the correct settings gives 5.
